parameter.name: FOLD_SINC_TAPS
parameter.what: the half-width, in samples, of the Hann-windowed sinc kernel `_fold_at` reads a fold row with when the fold period is not a whole number of samples. Registered with the proposal that introduced it (#767), not after it landed: the repair replaces `round()` -- and a rounding is a value nobody swept, the same shape as the epsilon dphase-ar1-floor replaced. -1 is not a width; it selects the integer-lag fold that shipped BEFORE the repair, and is on the grid so the sweep prices the repair itself rather than only the dial inside it.

objective.name: worst 44.1k<->48k gap in jit.cycledshape.seg0
objective.why: the defect the dial exists to fix, stated as the quantity test_extra_features_are_rate_independent measures: the reference corpus is 44.1 kHz and our renders are 48 kHz, so a column that moves between them on the SAME clip is partly a sample-rate detector. Worst over 44 values of f0 and BOTH resampling directions, because the three rows #767 was filed with turned out to be a property of which f0 values the test panel held. It is deliberately NOT the only thing the dial trades: a fold that aligned every row to the waveform would drive this to zero by destroying what the columns exist to see, and sees_jit in the same artefact is the constraint from that side.

range_basis: Doubling widths from 1 to 32, which brackets the two quantities the kernel has to sit between: the error it must remove is up to half a sample of row position, and the clip it reads is 0.24 s long, so a kernel wide enough to matter at the ends (32 samples is 0.7 ms) is the top of the useful range by construction rather than by result.

-1 is the behaviour that shipped before #767: `_fold` at an integer lag. It is on the grid so the record prices the repair and not only the dial, exactly as 0 is on dphase-ar1-floor's grid for the epsilon that preceded it.

0 is a fractional fold read by NEAREST SAMPLE -- the row alignment fixed, the sub-sample read not. It separates the two halves of the repair, which are otherwise confounded: it is on the grid so 'aligning the rows' and 'interpolating the read' get their own rows rather than one combined claim.

decision_rule.why: the decision this dial serves is whether a width changes what the rate-independence control can see, so the threshold comes from that control's own granularity, twice over. RATE_TOL_REL is 0.12 -- the control calls two numbers the same when they are within 12 % -- so 10 % is strictly tighter than the control's relative resolution. And RATE_TOL_ABS['ratio'] is 0.02, while this objective never exceeds 0.19 anywhere on the grid, so 10 % relative is at most 0.019 absolute, also tighter than the control's floor. Tighter is the conservative direction: a rule finer than the control can split points the control would call equal, which can only add groups, never manufacture a plateau.

evidence.instrument: mpd_features and jitter_features themselves, through their `taps` override -- the shipped fold, not a reimplementation of it, and tools/probes/test_fold_rate_sweep.py asserts that the probe's reading of a clip is identical to what extra_features puts in the vector. Stimuli are the module's own _square and its band-limited _resample, so the rate pair is the one the rate-independence test compares. Pairs where `dominant_period` picks a different OCTAVE at the two rates are REFUSED rather than scored: the two sides are then not measuring the same partial, and a fold-geometry gap read off them is not about fold geometry. Three of the 88 pairs per width are refused on that ground. Measured on python 3.12.3 / numpy 2.5.2 / scipy 1.18.1.
evidence.detail: the same artefact carries mpd_gap (the other fold family), n_over (how many columns are over tolerance anywhere on the grid), refused, walks and sees_jit. tools/sensitivity.py reads only the objective column; the rest are what it cannot see, and the verdict below is read against them.

prediction.basis: Stated from four quantities, none of which is a point on this sweep. (a) The integer fold starts row i at i*(pr-p) samples out, and a 0.24 s clip at 440 Hz holds about 100 rows, so its misalignment is tens of samples -- a large fraction of a period, and nothing a kernel width can be compared with. (b) A nearest-sample read bounds the error at half a sample per READ, but applies it independently at every column of the row; `_square`'s edges are one sample wide, so at an edge that is a full-scale error, and 0 must therefore be in the same league as -1 rather than with the interpolating widths. It is the only point on the grid where the objective can be WORSE than the thing it replaces, and nothing about doubling a kernel predicts which side of -1 it lands on. (c) Between 1 and 8 each step doubles the kernel on a signal whose spectrum reaches 0.45*sr, where a Hann-windowed sinc's residual falls steeply with width, so no two of those can agree to 10 %. (d) At the top the dial stops buying, because the kernel's own error drops below two residuals it cannot touch: the resampler's band-limiting, which this module already measures at ~0.8 ppm of phase and which _bl_square isolates, and the clip ends, where a WIDER kernel reads more zero padding and is therefore slightly worse. So the last two widths must be one group and it must be the last one, and the objective must stop falling before the grid does.

verdict.summary: The dial is a staircase that stops: 0.159 ratio of rate gap on the integer fold that shipped before #767, 0.186 on a nearest-sample read of the right rows -- WORSE than what it replaces, which is the one place the sweep contradicts the obvious story -- then 0.116, 0.055, 0.030, 0.018 and 0.014 as the kernel doubles, and 0.0147 at 32, where it has turned back up. Six of the eight widths are their own group at 10 %, so this is not a dial anyone may argue about without measuring; the only free choice is between 16 and 32, and 16 is the shipped value because the other three columns of the artefact do not prefer 32 either (n_over is 2 at both, sees_jit 0.0146 against 0.0148, walks 6 at both) and a narrower kernel reads less of the zero padding at the clip ends. 8 is NOT in that group and is the point the margin argument turns on: 0.0181 is only 10 % below the 0.0200 the control calls a difference, where 16 is 29 % below it.

limits: The objective alone is not a sufficient criterion for this dial and the record says so twice on purpose. tools/sensitivity.py reads only rate_gap; sees_jit in the same artefact is what that cannot see. It is how far jit.cyclecorr falls between a stable square and a 0.5 %-jittered one, and it FELL when the repair landed -- 0.0207 on the integer fold, 0.0146 at the shipped width -- because part of the old separation was the row walk this repair removes, not the oscillator. That is the repair working, but it is also the dial's cost, and test_jitter_separates_a_stable_oscillator_from_a_drifting_one now reads the margin against the same column's own 44.1k<->48k reproducibility (0.0002) rather than against the unanchored 0.02 it used to use.

The prediction above was written after the sweep ran. Its basis consults no point on the sweep, which is what makes it a prediction and not a transcription, but the honest claim is that it is derivable without the measurement, not that it was derived before it. The 16->32 step is the tightest thing it asserts -- the two differ by 3.5 %, against a 10 % rule -- so that group is where it would break first, on another numpy or another f0 grid.

88 pairs per width is 44 values of f0 in two directions, and 3 of them are REFUSED rather than scored because `dominant_period` picks a different octave at the two rates (850, 875 and 880 Hz built at 48 kHz and resampled down). The objective therefore says nothing about those clips at any width, which is correct -- the gap there is not fold geometry -- but it does mean the dial is unpriced against that second defect. It is carried as test_dominant_period_picks_a_different_octave_at_the_two_rates and filed separately.

The dp_err column of the detail tables is read against the NOMINAL f0, and `_square` quantises its period to the build rate's grid, so at the build rates where that rounding is large the diagnostic understates the misalignment (900 Hz built at 48 kHz emits 53-sample periods, i.e. 905.66 Hz, and dp_err reads 0.0000). It is a diagnostic, not the objective; the objective is measured on the columns themselves.

The panel is synthetic squares and tones, not corpus audio, and the whole sweep is one clip length (0.24 s) and one decay (80 ms). Whether a wider kernel's zero-padded ends matter more on a shorter clip is not measured here. The reference corpus is not on this host.

One residual survives the best width on this grid and it is not the dial's: 200 Hz built at 48 kHz leaves mpd2.50ms.rowcorr at 0.131 against a 0.120 tolerance, because 2.5 ms is exactly half that period so rowcorr saturates at -1.0000 and the two sides differ by `_square`'s hard edges rather than by the fold. test_the_one_residual_the_fold_repair_cannot_reach_is_the_stimulus carries the control (`_bl_square`, band-limited identically at both rates, comes back at 0.0004).
